slot.brief: Given i for an electrolyte or compare i values across dissociation/association cases; ask which solution shows maximum boiling point elevation at same molality

stem: At equal molality in the same solvent, which electrolyte solution has the greatest boiling-point elevation? The degree of dissociation, $\alpha$, is given.

verdicts.working: For dissociation into n ions, i = 1 + α(n − 1). The van’t Hoff factors are A: 2.0, B: 2.6, C: 2.2, D: 2.5. Since ΔTb = iKb m, B has the greatest elevation.

working:
$\Delta T_b=iK_bm$; at equal $K_b,m$, compare $i$. 
$\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4,\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4,\text{CaCl}_2$: $i=1+2\alpha=2.00,2.60,2.20$. 
$\text{AlCl}_3$: $i=1+3\alpha=2.50$. 
Maximum: $i=2.60$.

Independent check: For dissociation into n ions, i = 1 + α(n − 1). The van’t Hoff factors are A: 2.0, B: 2.6, C: 2.2, D: 2.5. Since ΔTb = iKb m, B has the greatest elevation.
solution:
Boiling-point elevation is $4T_b=iK_bm4$, so at equal molality and in the same solvent, compare $i=1+\alpha(n-1)$.
For (A), (B), (C), and (D), $i=2.00, 2.60, 2.20,$ and $2.50$, respectively.
The greatest value is $i=2.60$ for (B), $4\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_44$.
